exposure: Resident experience as primary surgeon in specific complex obstetric procedures (Forceps-assisted vaginal delivery, vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery, cerclage, breech second twin, breech delivery, perineal repairs, cesarean hysterectomy)
outcome: Resident comfort performing complex obstetric procedures independently
Resident comfort performing complex obstetric procedures postresidency
cohort: The study participants were 417 OB/GYN residents across the United States who completed an anonymous e-survey in March 2018.
finding: Many graduating OB/GYN residents in the United States may not feel comfortable performing several complex obstetric procedures independently despite ACGME recommendations.
mod_finding: All 4th-year residents felt comfortable performing operative vaginal deliveries (VAVD or FAVD) postresidency, however, 17% were uncomfortable with 4th-degree repairs, 33% with cesarean hysterectomy, 28% with breech second twin, and 74% with breech vaginal delivery postresidency.
